content.note: poverty_guidelines: HHS 2025 Poverty Guidelines (90 FR 5917, Jan 17 2025); the guidelines in effect at open enrollment govern 2026 coverage-year premium tax credits (26 CFR 1.36B-1(h)).
applicable_percentages: Rev. Proc. 2025-25 (2026 applicable percentage table under IRC 36B(b)(3)(A)); enhanced ARPA/IRA percentages expired after 2025, so credits end above 400% of the poverty line.

age_curve: Federal default standard age curve, 45 CFR 147.102(e) and CMS Final Guidance Regarding Age Curves and State Reporting (Dec 16 2016, effective 2018). Transcribed from that guidance; verify_against_cms_appendix_i=true means the table was not re-checked against the published PDF for this release.

medicare: CMS 2026 Medicare Parts A & B premiums and deductibles and Part D IRMAA (CMS-8089-N, CMS-8090-N, CMS-8091-N, Nov 2025). IRMAA uses MAGI from two years prior; the top tier thresholds ($500,000/$750,000) are frozen through 2027 by 42 USC 1395r(i)(6).

content.figure: Full monthly premium, fewer than 30 quarters of coverage
content.source: CMS fact sheet, 2026 Medicare Parts A & B premiums and deductibles (https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/2026-medicare-parts-b-premiums-deductibles); the CY 2026 Part A premium notice is CMS-8089-N

content.figure: Reduced monthly premium, 30 to 39 quarters of coverage
content.source: Same CMS fact sheet (https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/fact-sheets/2026-medicare-parts-b-premiums-deductibles); the reduction is 45% of the full premium under 42 USC 1395i-2(d)(4) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1395i-2)

content.value: 40 or more (own or a qualifying spouse's record)

content.note: Cross-check: 55% of $565 is $310.75, which CMS rounds to $311.
